lines.text: | worth, weighed higher | Pro 3:15; Job 28:16; 1Pe 1:7; Psa 36:7 | what it is weighed against: every desire, gold, perishing gold |
| rare | 1Sa 3:1; Pro 25:17 (*seldom*); Isa 13:12 (route C) | rarity of the word; a visit kept rare |
| splendour | Job 31:26; Psa 37:20 | splendour that entices a heart; splendour that vanishes |
| costly | 1Ki 5:17; 7:9–11 (route C); Dan 11:38 | what is given, and to whom |
| honour, esteem | 1Sa 18:30; Act 5:34; Heb 13:4 | who gives it and who withholds it |
| a price set | Zec 11:13 | a price that is an insult ("lordly", in irony) |
| dear | Jer 31:20 | dear while spoken against |
- **Above every desire:** Pro 3:15. The scale has all of a person's wants on the other side, not only jewels. 10.6 had quoted only the second half; the word itself was not carried.
- **Not known:** Job 28:13, 16. Proverbs states the worth; Job says man does not know it. **I read** the two together as worth and blindness to it, not as contradiction.
- **Shown by trial:** 1Pe 1:6–8. Grief, love and joy toward one not seen, in three verses. Gold is tested and perishes; faith is tested and found.
- **Making a person wait:** Jam 5:7–8 against 5:3–5. **I read** two hearts: fattened on hoarded treasure, or established by waiting.
- **A refuge:** Isa 28:15–16; 1Pe 2:6–7. Lies as refuge against the precious stone; "not in haste".
| 1Ch 29:2–3 | David | God's house | "because of my devotion" |
| Dan 11:37–38 | the self-magnifying king | a god of fortresses | the same kind of gift. **I read** he honours the strength he wants |
| 1Ki 10:1–13 (2Ch 9:9 carried) | the queen of Sheba | Solomon | she came to test; "there was no more breath in her"; she gave after she saw, and was given all she desired |
| Heb 13:4–5 | all | marriage held in honour | set beside "free from love of money", with his presence as the ground of contentment |
| 1Sa 18:29–30 | the people | David's name esteemed | Saul's fear in the verse before |
- **Entices:** Job 31:24–28. The moon's splendour, a heart "secretly enticed", a kiss of the hand, counted as falseness to God. **I read** eye, heart and mouth in one sentence.
- **Passes:** Psa 37:20, in the psalm that opens "be not envious". **I read** the figure as an answer to envy.
- **Covers:** Rev 17:4. A golden cup full of what is unclean.
- **Turns to pride:** Eze 28:13–17. A given covering, blamelessness, then trade, violence and a proud heart (Ch 12, beside Eze 28:2 and 31:9–10).
- **Two ways to fill a house:** Pro 1:13 (plunder) and 24:3–4 (knowledge), the second in the chapter that opens on envy of evil men (24:1–2). Pro 12:27: the slothful does not roast what he caught.
- **The cargo ends in souls:** Rev 18:11–17. **I read** the merchants' grief as for the trade, not for the souls in the cargo.
| 1Sa 3:1–9 | 10.2 | the word rare; Samuel did not yet know the Lord; Eli perceived it and taught the answer. **I read** hearing that had to be learned |
| Pro 25:16–17 | 10.10 | the neighbour set beside honey |
| Jer 15:18–19 | 10.5 | after the complaint, "If you return … if you utter what is precious, and not what is worthless" |
| Zec 11:12–13; Mat 27:3, 9 | 10.4 *It reckons* | the lordly price |
| Act 5:34 | 10.13 | Gamaliel "held in honor by all the people" added to the verse already cited |

- **Jer 31:18–20:** Ephraim's grief and shame, then "Is Ephraim my dear son? … as often as I speak against him, I do remember him still. Therefore my heart yearns for him". Speaking against and remembering together; the yearning given as the ground of mercy.
- **1Pe 1:18–19:** ransomed from "futile ways inherited", not with silver or gold, but with "the precious blood of Christ". Set beside Isa 43:4, which is already in 13.1.
- **Carried:** 2Ch 9:9 (by 1Ki 10:10).

- **Route C (14):** 2Sa 12:30; 1Ch 20:2 (a stone in a crown); 1Ki 10:11; 2Ch 9:10; Eze 27:22 (cargo and trade); 1Ki 5:17; 7:9, 10, 11; 2Ch 3:6 (building stones); Rev 21:11, 19 (the city's radiance and foundations); Zec 14:6 ("cold"); Isa 13:12 (people made "rare", few left). In each the word describes a thing, and no inner act is stated.
